items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: The interviewee only responds to the interviewer's story about Perry Coleman with 'A coincidence.' There is no evidence the interviewee personally knew or met Perry Coleman.

ctx.x: Well, I told Archie, Archie Levinson has, he's the publisher, and I told him one day, I said, why don't we put my original lyric back on there? So, he said, well, he says, I don't know, we got it printed up and everything and they might release it someday. I said, I don't think they'll release it because it's similar to the titles. I'm still, I'm gonna still see them because the tune is a beautiful tune. I got it on the tape here, I want you to hear it.

Well, this, this boy that I used to work with, this Italian boy, he wrote a song and he asked me to, in fact, you took it down. Uh-huh. And, uh, it was real fine. And, uh, I was playing some records over one day at my house and I ran into Perry Coleman and he sang the same number, just a different title, different record. It was so close together you couldn't tell. Yeah. We never had heard it.
A coincidence. A coincidence. Just a thousand of miles away and direct coincidence like that.
